_note: ENCOUNTERS — the P11 format, shaped by slice ruling 4 (2026-08-23): combat is simulated and toggleable, so an encounter collapses to a difficulty-ranked row with an enemy list. The full scripted form exists ONLY for the prologue battles, which are fixed by design and precede the map. Authored 2026-08-25 from ENEMY-REVIEW.md. FORMAT IS PROPOSED, NOT RULED — this is the sketch for review.

format.sliceRow: id · difficulty (an integer rank the battle list is sorted by) · enemies (unit ids with counts) · powerSources (optional: the battle's external pool and any scheduled gains) · terrainHint (optional). Nothing else — ruling 4 means no maps, no scripting for slice battles.
format.prologueBattle: The five fixed battles carry the full shape: setup (placed units by zone), schedule (phase-keyed spawns by edge), loseAfter, retreat, civilians, events. CLOCK RULING 2026-08-23: schedules count PHASES — the word turn never appears in encounter data. Placement is by hex — see format.placement.
format.powerSources: kind: external (pool at battle start) | arrival (one-time +X when a unit enters, stays in the pool after its death) | clock (per-phase or conditional gains live on the unit rows themselves — the Lieutenant's EOT, the Vampire Lord's kills).
format.placement: HEX PLACEMENT, ruled 2026-08-25 (zones were vagueries): at:{col,row} places on that hex; at:{near:{col,row},range:N} deploys anywhere within N of it; at:{oneOf:[{col,row},...]} is a scripted either/or. Multi-unit entries list one hex per unit in `hexes`. BOARD: every row carries `board: {width,height}` (PROVING-PLAN Stage A3, 2026-09-04) and must be one of the four ruled formats; all ten are 16x16 standard today. AXIS, RE-AUTHORED 2026-09-04 — heroes deploy WEST (low col) and enemies EAST (high col), per the ruling "Heroes start on the left, and enemies start on the right. That is the default configuration." Every placement in this file was rotated ninety degrees to match: col=(15-oldRow), row=oldCol. That is a ROTATION, not a transpose — transposing would have sent the old enemy edge (row 0) to col 0, which is the hero side. The old zone word is kept as `was` for provenance; the hex is authoritative. SUPERSEDED: this note used to say "row 0 = enemy edge, row 15 = player edge", and used to say hex.ts had WIDTH=HEIGHT=12 and needed updating by the engine. Both are gone — the engine reads the board off the map (engine 4932fde).
format.scriptedEncounter: id · name · setup (units on the board at the start) · schedule (waves by PHASE, each naming units, counts and where they enter). A THIRD kind, first written 2026-09-02: it has a phase script like a prologue battle but is not one of the five, and it carries no hex placements because none were dictated — the sides are named in prose until it gets a board.

Ruled 2026-08-25: Farmer, School Teacher and School Children are confirmed in place as civilian units. The dictated Lumberjack maps to hero.fixed.lumberjack-and-wife (the row that exists). ART: all six have legacy thumbnails in the Codex today; full art exists in hell-tcg New Art/hero-art/ as UNDECLARED v1/v2 pairs (farmer-family, farmer-group, lumberjack, orphan-child, school-child) plus settled schoolteacher and school-children files — picking v1 vs v2 is an art ruling per gen/art-conventions.json, not a guess, and local card/ folders for teacher/children are empty pending the art channel. 2026-09-28 (engine DECISIONS.md, Andrew): "Second battle is Lumberjack and wife. They're two different units." hero.fixed.lumberjack-and-wife is the Lumberjack alone; the Wife is hero.fixed.lumberjacks-wife, confirmed as a civilian unit (content.opening-units).

scripted.name: Horrors of the Night

setup.was: far side — hex placement added 2026-09-03 with the far-side ruling

schedule.note: nothing arrives — the quiet phase, and the one where the darkness the Eyeblights left does the work

spawn.was: the opposite side — RULED 2026-09-03 to mean the ENEMY side, i.e. the far edge, as everything else
the opposite side — the enemy side

scripted.intent: The board goes dark faster than the party can cross it. Four Eyeblights strip Vision from range 9 and each one that dies floods ten hexes with darkness — then the things that live in darkness arrive.
scripted.source: Dictated 2026-09-02. PHASE NUMBERING IS A READING: dictated as 'next phase ... in the second phase, or their first end phase, there is nothing ... the next one ... the next one', read as waves at the end of phases 1, 2 (empty), 3 and 4. Say so if the empty phase sits elsewhere. No hex placements were dictated beyond the last wave arriving from the opposite side. | 2026-09-03 RULED: all units start on the FAR SIDE; the battle starts in darkness, every square dark; "from the opposite side" at phase 4 means the ENEMY side (the far edge), NOT behind the party. The darkness is not static: heroes light their Vision radius on their own phase, and the night family answers by stripping Vision and repainting darkness — that tug of war IS the encounter. Vision: stat 0, battlefield +6, floor 1.

standing.rule: THE BOARD STARTS DARK, AND LIGHT IS A TUG OF WAR
standing.effect: Every hex is dark at phase 1 (Darkness the battlefield condition, whole-map). On the HERO phase each hero lights everything within its Vision radius. The night family then strips Vision and repaints darkness over what was lit. Light is not a resource the party spends — it is a bubble that moves with them and that the enemy shrinks and paints over.
standing.source: Ruled 2026-09-03: "when it's the hero's turn, they light up everything within their vision range. Then things will attack and lower their vision range and try to repaint Nightfall."
standing.asData: condition: darkness (capability.vision, 2026-09-03) — the board starts dark, heroes light within Vision on the hero phase, the night family repaints

standing.effect: The Vision STAT is 0 by default — nothing is stored there. The battlefield contributes a +6 modifier. Effective Vision = 6 + whatever badges, gear and effects modify it. It can never fall below 1: every unit always sees its adjacent hexes.
standing.source: Ruled 2026-09-03: "the base modifier to vision range is 6... it should always have a minimum of one. Every unit can always see what is adjacent to it. But the base vision stats are zero because there's no reason to have a stat there, but the modifier to vision on the battlefield is 6." GENERAL RULE, not specific to this encounter — COMBAT-DESIGN.md sec4 is the owning document and carries it too.

authored.name: Orphanage
authored.note: The opening, battle 1 (engine DECISIONS.md 2026-09-28 'Battle 1 (Orphanage) redefined'): "We'll change the two zombies and a child to two zombies, an orphan child, and a school teacher. The orphan child and school teacher should be in two of the hexes to the left of the house, right next to the house. Zombies are going to start on the right edge. No retreat because you're surrounded. Turn 4, we're going to have a zombie arrive from the bottom edge to the immediate left of the water. Turn 5, we're going to have a zombie arrive from the left edge, center." Victory: clear the map (ruled the same day). No turn limit. Civilians are not objectives: their deaths do not end the battle. Hexes are the Abbotown Ground Check's markers (assets/battle-atlas/opening-ground-proposal-2026-09-28.json); the heroes' zone is Claude's reading (engine SWITCHES.md openingHeroZones). AMENDED 2026-09-28 (engine DECISIONS.md 'the Orphanage loses a Zombie at the start and a later one'): "Let's remove an early zombie and a later zombie." One Zombie at the start, (19,3), and one arrival, Turn 4's at (9,13); the (19,5) Zombie and Turn 5's from the left edge (0,6) are gone. Which of each is Claude's reading (engine SWITCHES.md openingOrphanageLighter). AMENDED 2026-09-29 (engine DECISIONS.md 'the Orphanage gains a Zombie on Turn 2 and one on Turn 3'): "Battle 1: Let's add a zombie on turn 2 and a zombie on turn 3." Turn 2's Zombie at (19,5) on the right edge and Turn 3's at (0,6), the left edge, centre; where each arrives is Claude's reading (engine SWITCHES.md openingOrphanageArrivals). AMENDED 2026-10-04 (engine DECISIONS.md 'the opening's tutorial: the first hero's class line, no map before battle 1, the Orphanage's lessons, the camera shows what arrives, new enemies are named, a closer start'): "We need to shrink this map. First we can bring the hero forward to the end of the bridge and bring the zombie left, maybe 3 squares. So that conflict is much faster." The heroes' zone moves from the west bank (5,4) to the bridge's east end: the lone hero on (10,5), the deck's last hex on the house's side, and the zone names its other hexes in order - dry ground east of it, (11,5), (11,4), (11,6), (12,5), (12,4) - so that no hero is deployed in the water beside the deck. The starting Zombie moves three hexes left, from (19,3) to (16,3). The board stays 20 by 14 and its ground is untouched ("shrink" is read as the distance); the civilians and the three arrivals stand. Which end of the bridge and which hexes are Claude's reading (engine SWITCHES.md openingHeroZones, closerStart*).
